From e7e921918d905544500ca7a95889f898121ba886 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Amit Sunil Dhamne <amitsd@google.com>
Date: Tue, 14 May 2024 15:01:31 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] usb: typec: tcpm: fix use-after-free case in
 tcpm_register_source_caps

There could be a potential use-after-free case in
tcpm_register_source_caps(). This could happen when:
 * new (say invalid) source caps are advertised
 * the existing source caps are unregistered
 * tcpm_register_source_caps() returns with an error as
   usb_power_delivery_register_capabilities() fails

This causes port->partner_source_caps to hold on to the now freed source
caps.

Reset port->partner_source_caps value to NULL after unregistering
existing source caps.

Fixes: 230ecdf71a64 ("usb: typec: tcpm: unregister existing source caps before re-registration")
Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Signed-off-by: Amit Sunil Dhamne <amitsd@google.com>
Reviewed-by: Ondrej Jirman <megi@xff.cz>
Reviewed-by: Heikki Krogerus <heikki.krogerus@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Dmitry Baryshkov <dmitry.baryshkov@linaro.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240514220134.2143181-1-amitsd@google.com
Signed-off-by: Greg Kroah-Hartman <gregkh@linuxfoundation.org>

diff --git a/drivers/usb/typec/tcpm/tcpm.c b/drivers/usb/typec/tcpm/tcpm.c
index 8a1af08f71b6..be4127ef84e9 100644
--- a/drivers/usb/typec/tcpm/tcpm.c
+++ b/drivers/usb/typec/tcpm/tcpm.c
@@ -3014,8 +3014,10 @@ static int tcpm_register_source_caps(struct tcpm_port *port)
 	memcpy(caps.pdo, port->source_caps, sizeof(u32) * port->nr_source_caps);
 	caps.role = TYPEC_SOURCE;
 
-	if (cap)
+	if (cap) {
 		usb_power_delivery_unregister_capabilities(cap);
+		port->partner_source_caps = NULL;
+	}
 
 	cap = usb_power_delivery_register_capabilities(port->partner_pd, &caps);
 	if (IS_ERR(cap))
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/usb/typec/tcpm/tcpm.c`**
- In the function `tcpm_register_source_caps`, a new line was added to set `port->partner_source_caps` to `NULL` after unregistering existing source capabilities with `usb_power_delivery_unregister_capabilities(cap)`. This change ensures that the pointer does not hold onto a reference to freed memory, thus preventing a potential use-after-free scenario.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a specific bug related to the handling of source capabilities in the `tcpm_register_source_caps` function. The change is directly related to the previous commit identified by the fix tag (`Fixes: 230ecdf71a64`), which introduced the unregistering of existing source capabilities. The new line added in this patch ensures that after unregistering, the pointer to the source capabilities is reset to `NULL`, thereby preventing any accidental access to freed memory in case of an error during re-registration. This is a critical fix to enhance the stability and safety of the code.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
usb_power_delivery_unregister_capabilities(cap);
```
```c
cap = usb_power_delivery_register_capabilities(port->partner_pd, &caps);
```
```c
port->partner_source_caps = cap;
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because when `usb_power_delivery_unregister_capabilities(cap)` is called, it frees the memory associated with `cap`. If the subsequent call to `usb_power_delivery_register_capabilities` fails, `port->partner_source_caps` still holds a reference to the now-freed memory, leading to a use-after-free condition when accessed later.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
port->partner_source_caps = NULL;
```
```c
if (cap) {
```
Reason:
The fix involves setting `port->partner_source_caps` to `NULL` after unregistering the existing source capabilities. This ensures that if the re-registration fails, `port->partner_source_caps` does not point to freed memory, thus preventing any potential use-after-free issues.
